cards.explanation: The answer is a palace for David. Hiram, king of Tyre, sent envoys, cedar logs, stonemasons and carpenters to build it (1 Chronicles 14:1). That's a whole crew showing up at the door, friends, and some of us can't even get a repair person to call us back.

The answer is people. David realized the LORD had established him as king "…for the sake of His people Israel." (1 Chronicles 14:2). I love that he saw it that way, friends. The kingdom wasn't about David showing off. It was for the sake of God's people.

The answer is False. When the Philistines went searching for David, he learned of it and "…went out to face them." (1 Chronicles 14:8). No hiding, no waiting for them to go home. Picture me hearing trouble was looking for me, friends. I'd be under the counter.

The answer is that he asks God what to do. David inquired of God: "Should I go up against the Philistines? Will You deliver them into my hand?" (1 Chronicles 14:10). He asked before he moved, friends. I wish I'd asked before I tried baking a batch with the oven off.

The answer is True. David asked, and the LORD answered, "Go... for I will deliver them into your hand" (1 Chronicles 14:10). A clear yes and a promise, friends. You don't get a better answer than that.

The answer is False. David said, "Like a bursting flood, God has burst out against my enemies by my hand." (1 Chronicles 14:11). The credit went to God, and the place was named Baal-perazim after it. I'd have been tempted to put my own name on the cookie box, friends.
The answer is their gods. The text says, "There the Philistines abandoned their gods…" (1 Chronicles 14:12). They left them there at Baal-perazim, where David had defeated them.

The answer is burned in the fire. The text says, "…David ordered that they be burned in the fire." (1 Chronicles 14:12). The Philistines had abandoned those gods there, and David gave the order about them, friends. Fire was the answer.

The answer is False. The text says, "…David again inquired of God…" (1 Chronicles 14:14). Having won once, he asked again anyway, friends. God answered with a plan: don't march up after them, but circle around and attack in front of the balsam trees.

The answer is to circle around and attack by the balsam trees. God said, "Do not march up after them, but circle around them and attack them in front of the balsam trees." (1 Chronicles 14:14). It's a different plan from the first battle, friends, so I'm glad David asked again.

The answer is to move out to battle. God said, "As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move out to battle…" (1 Chronicles 14:15). Hear the sound, then go, friends. Think of the moment your oven timer dings and you reach for the mitts.

The answer is that God has gone out ahead of him. God said the sound would mean "…that God has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines." (1 Chronicles 14:15). David was told to listen for it, friends. The sound in the treetops was a sign that God was already on the move.

The answer is True. The text says, "…David did as God had commanded him…" (1 Chronicles 14:16). He followed the plan and the signal he was given, friends. They struck down the Philistine army all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.

The answer is LORD. The verse says, "And David’s fame went out into every land, and the LORD caused all nations to fear him." (1 Chronicles 14:17). His fame went out into every land, friends. The part about the nations fearing him is the LORD's doing.
